modifications.problem: Missing values in Age (20% of rows)
modifications.impact: Biases demographic analyses, segmentation, and any age‑based modeling such as churn prediction.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Age using the median age of customers within the same ProductCategory and StoreLocation; if both groupings are unavailable, fall back to the overall median age.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Dropping rows (would lose 20% of data), imputing with overall mean (sensitive to outliers), using predictive modeling (adds complexity and risk of over‑fitting for a single column).
modifications.effect: Approximately 20% of rows will have their Age column filled; no rows are removed. The Age column type remains float64.

modifications.problem: Missing values in Amount (10% of rows)
modifications.impact: Underestimates total revenue and distorts average transaction size calculations, affecting financial reporting and forecasting.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Amount with the mean transaction amount for the matching ProductCategory and StoreLocation; fallback to overall mean Amount when group statistics are unavailable.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Dropping rows (would lose 10% of sales data), zero‑imputation (would artificially deflate revenue), predictive regression imputation (adds model risk for a numeric target).
modifications.effect: Approximately 10% of rows receive a numeric Amount value; column type stays float64.

modifications.problem: Missing values in FeedbackScore (10% of rows)
modifications.impact: Skews customer satisfaction metrics, potentially misleading NPS calculations and service improvement initiatives.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute using the median FeedbackScore within the same ProductCategory and IsReturned flag (returned vs not returned); fallback to overall median FeedbackScore.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Dropping rows (loss of feedback data), filling with a constant (e.g., 0) which would artificially lower scores, complex predictive modeling (unnecessary for a single rating column).
modifications.effect: Approximately 10% of rows get a median‑based FeedbackScore; column remains float64.

modifications.impact: Prevents proper chronological sorting, time‑based aggregations, and seasonal analyses.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Convert Date column to datetime using pandas.to_datetime with errors='coerce'. Any unparsable entries become NaT and are later reviewed manually.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Leaving as object (blocks time calculations), custom regex parsing (unnecessary when to_datetime handles most formats).
modifications.effect: All rows retain their Date value; type changes from object to datetime64[ns]. Potentially a few rows flagged for manual review if NaT appears.

modifications.impact: Compromises row uniqueness, downstream joins, and any transaction‑level analytics.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Run a uniqueness check; if duplicates exist, keep the first occurrence, flag subsequent duplicates in a new column 'DuplicateFlag', and log TransactionIDs for audit.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Automatic deletion of all duplicates (risk of losing valid data), generating new IDs (breaks original audit trail).
modifications.effect: No rows are removed; a boolean DuplicateFlag column is added. Primary key integrity is restored for analysis.

modifications.problem: Inconsistent categorical values in Gender (case/spacing variations)
modifications.impact: Leads to fragmented group counts and inaccurate gender‑based segmentation.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Standardize Gender values to title case ('Male', 'Female', 'Other') and map unknown or blank entries to 'Unknown'.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Dropping the column (loss of demographic insight), one‑hot encoding before standardization (would propagate errors).
modifications.effect: All rows retain Gender; values become consistent. No rows are removed.

target_associations.IsReturned: Highly imbalanced (80% false). No direct correlation metrics provided, but the low return rate combined with skewed Amount suggests returns may be concentrated among higher‑value purchases—requires further investigation.
target_associations.FeedbackScore: Negatively correlated with Amount (r = -0.33) and positively with Age (r = 0.20). Younger, higher‑spending customers tend to give lower scores, while older shoppers give slightly higher scores.
target_associations.Amount: Negatively correlated with Age (r = -0.28) and FeedbackScore (r = -0.33). Older customers and those providing higher feedback scores tend to have lower transaction values.
